name: Lowell Reynolds
bio: Lowell Andre Reynolds is a Nashville-based music producer and audio engineer who holds a business degree and is studying law at Syracuse University College of Law. He was born in Florida and raised in Indiana. He is running as an independent for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District after earlier considering the 5th district.

platform.point: Wants to restore checks and balances and limit executive overreach.
Presents himself as unaffiliated with either party, putting the Constitution and individual liberty first.
Aims to shift power from Washington back to citizens and hold leaders accountable.

notes: Campaign site is hosted on a WordPress staging address and lists no detailed issue positions.

name: David Kustoff
bio: David Kustoff has represented Tennessee's 8th Congressional District since 2017. A Memphis native and attorney, he served as U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee from 2006 to 2008. He holds business and law degrees from the University of Memphis.

platform.point: Supports advancing President Trump's policy agenda in Congress.
Wants to end illegal immigration and secure the border.
Prioritises law and order and cooperation among local, state and federal law enforcement.
Focuses on fighting terrorism and giving service members the tools they need.
Pledges to strengthen the rural economy and advocate for West Tennessee farmers.
Holds that life begins at conception and backs pro-life policies.

economy.evidence: Supports lower taxes, backed cutting the corporate rate to 21%, and opposes over-regulation.

welfare.evidence: Voted for the 2017 American Health Care Act and supports repealing the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion without exceptions and same-sex marriage (voted against the Respect for Marriage Act), while backing gun rights and opposing background-check expansion.

security.evidence: Former U.S. Attorney who backs strict punishment and opposes sentencing reform that he says compromises public safety.

immigration.evidence: Supports a border wall, enforcing existing immigration law, and backed the 2017 travel ban.

foreign.evidence: Favors military action against ISIS and a superior nuclear arsenal, and emphasizes U.S. global leadership.

energy.evidence: Opposes government green-energy development and supports deregulating domestic oil exploration.

education.evidence: Opposes Common Core and favors local control of education.

faith.evidence: Supports protecting religious liberty, including religious exemptions for businesses.

notes: Tech score (30) was dropped to null for lack of citable evidence; security was filled from his law-and-order record rather than surveillance votes.

name: Heidi Kuhn
bio: Heidi Kuhn is the Shelby County Criminal Court Clerk, with more than 26 years in government, and is from Memphis. Her office has expanded access to expungements, processing close to 10,000 of them. She was named Tennessee Clerk of the Year in 2025.

platform.point: Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $17 by 2030 and passing the PRO Act.
Would protect Medicare and Medicaid, cap prescription drug costs and fund rural hospitals.
Would vote to end the war in Iran.
Proposes pausing new data centers until communities have input and costs to ratepayers are transparent.
Opposes tariffs on farm equipment and backs a farm bill that prioritises small farmers and rural broadband.
Wants immigration enforcement to respect due process and seeks transparency on the local CoreCivic detention facility.

economy.evidence: Backs a $17 minimum wage, the PRO Act, and action against grocery and energy price gouging.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Medicare, Medicaid and SNAP, expand the child tax credit and cap drug costs.

immigration.evidence: Calls for due process and constitutional limits in ICE enforcement and scrutiny of detention facilities.

foreign.evidence: Would vote to end U.S. military involvement in Iran.

energy.evidence: Supports lowering energy costs through domestic production alongside limits on price gouging.

tech.evidence: Proposes a data-center moratorium pending community input and scrutiny of AI's effect on power bills.

notes: Campaign photo URL is a homepage header image and may not be a tight headshot.

name: Pamela Moses
bio: Pamela Jeanine Moses is a Memphis organizer and activist who founded Rise Up America in 2018 and leads a voting-access campaign. She formerly chaired the District 7 Shelby County Democratic Executive Committee. She studied political science at the University of Tennessee at Knoxville and holds a master's degree from Union University.

platform.point: Supports universal healthcare access and more mental health services in underserved areas.
Backs workforce programs for formerly incarcerated people and treatment rather than jail for substance use.
Calls for stricter rules on gun manufacturing and sales plus youth violence prevention programs.
Promotes green energy, carbon emission cuts and high-speed rail investment.
Proposes reparations of $50,000 per person or family for descendants of enslaved people.
Wants farmers' markets in food deserts and direct farm-to-consumer sales.

economy.evidence: Proposes federal reparations payments and public investment in high-speed rail and job training.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal healthcare access and expanded mental health services.

energy.evidence: Promotes green energy and carbon emission reduction strategies.

notes: Her campaign site redirects from pamelamoses.com and refers to both Congress and Senate. The campaign image may be a graphic rather than a plain headshot.

name: Justin J. Pearson
bio: Justin J. Pearson, a Memphis native, has represented District 86 in the Tennessee House of Representatives since 2023. He co-founded Memphis Community Against Pollution, which opposed the Byhalia Pipeline. He graduated from Bowdoin College and won the 2026 Democratic primary for the 9th district.

platform.point: Supports healthcare for all through Medicare for All.
Wants an economy that works for the many, including higher wages.
Opposes polluting data centers and prioritises environmental and climate justice.
Seeks to end gun violence, having proposed repealing permitless carry and creating red-flag orders.
Wants to get big money out of politics.
Aims for safe schools and streets and backed limits on rehiring officers with criminal records.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on an economy for the many and sponsored a higher minimum wage for state employees.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights but seeks gun restrictions such as repealing permitless carry and adding red-flag laws.

security.evidence: Proposed barring officers with criminal records from moving between departments and calls for dismantling ICE.

immigration.evidence: Calls for dismantling Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

energy.evidence: Led opposition to the Byhalia Pipeline and campaigns on climate justice and against polluting data centers.

notes: Liberty lowered from 75 to 50 because his support for abortion rights offsets his gun-restriction positions in the average; security was newly filled from policing and ICE positions.

name: Brent Taylor
bio: Brent Taylor has represented District 31 in the Tennessee Senate since 2023. He served 12 years on the Memphis City Council starting in 1995 and later on the Shelby County Commission and election commission. He is a funeral director who co-founded a family-owned funeral business in the Memphis area.

platform.point: Makes crime reduction in Shelby County his central focus, including work with the Memphis Safe Task Force.
Backs a state constitutional amendment to deny bail for the most serious violent crimes.
Campaigns on making Memphis matter in Washington.
Says he supports President Trump's agenda.
Says he has repeatedly defended the constitutional right to bear arms.
Highlights that he never voted for a tax increase on the city council and backs small-business legislation.

economy.evidence: Says he never voted to raise taxes and has supported business-friendly legislation.

security.evidence: Sponsored juvenile-crime bills and backed a state constitutional amendment to deny bail for major violent crimes.

notes: Economy score is newly added from his campaign biography; other positions beyond crime are thinly documented.
